info.name: SOA Tourism
info.description: Exercises the gateway's critical endpoints end-to-end: auth flow, the progressive login-throttling demo, and the checkout/shopping-cart path. Import the companion environment (SOA-Tourism.postman_environment.json) and select it before running anything. Run 'Auth - Happy Path' first (top to bottom) to populate {{accessToken}} - it has no side effects, so leave it be and go run every other folder freely. 'Auth - Session Lifecycle' is separate on purpose: Refresh/Change Password/Logout each invalidate something (see each request's own description) - run those deliberately, and Logout only when you're completely done.

item.name: Auth - Happy Path
item.description: Run these 3 top-to-bottom, once, to get a valid session. Nothing here has a side effect on your accessToken/refreshToken - safe to leave as-is while you run every other folder below. When you're fully done testing, run 'Auth - Session Lifecycle' > 'Logout' as the very last thing.

exec: // A fresh random username each run, so re-running the collection never hits 409 Conflict.

item.name: Auth - Session Lifecycle (each of these has a side effect - read before running)
item.description: Everything here changes your session state. Run these deliberately, one at a time, never as a batch/Runner pass - and run 'Logout' dead last, only when you're completely done testing everything else.

item.name: Refresh token (rotates both tokens - old refreshToken dies)
item.description: Refresh tokens are single-use: the server issues a brand new accessToken+refreshToken pair and immediately revokes the one you sent. The test script above updates the collection variables for you - but if you ever run this from the Collection Runner (not just Send), double-check the variables actually got saved back to the collection afterward before relying on them elsewhere.

item.name: Change password (revokes ALL refresh tokens, accessToken still fine)
item.description: Setting newPassword back to the same value keeps this request idempotent to re-run. This revokes every refresh token for the account server-side (so other logged-in sessions can't keep using the old credentials' trust) - your current accessToken keeps working until it naturally expires (15 min from issuance), but {{refreshToken}} becomes useless immediately after this runs, even though the collection variable still holds the old value.

item.name: Logout (revokes ONLY the current refreshToken - accessToken still valid until it expires)
item.description: Verified empirically against this stack: logout only calls tokenRepo.RevokeRefreshToken on the one refresh token you send - it does NOT touch the access token (stateless JWT, no blacklist). A profile call with the same accessToken right after logout still returns 200; only a subsequent /refresh with that refreshToken returns 401. So after Logout, everything using {{accessToken}} in this collection keeps working fine until 15 minutes after you last logged in/refreshed - it just LOOKS broken if you assume logout kills the bearer token the way it would in a session-cookie system. Run this last.

exec: console.log('This stack has no email service - the token is returned directly in the response for local testing only.');

item.name: Throttling Demo (progressive login backoff)
item.description: Run 'Login - wrong password' with Postman's Collection Runner (or just click Send repeatedly) against a real username - e.g. {{testUsername}} after running 'Auth - Happy Path' once. First 2 failures return 401 for free; every failure after that locks the identity out for an exponentially growing window (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, ... capped at 15 min) - visible as HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Wait out each Retry-After before the next send to see it escalate; spamming during a lockout does NOT extend it further (see the backend code comment for why) - each additional 429 just reports the same lockout counting down.

item.name: Content Creation (guide)
item.description: Needs a guide-role account. 'Auth - Happy Path' registers a tourist by default - run '1. Register (tourist)' once with role changed to "guide" in the body (or register a second account by hand) and put its accessToken here as {{guideAccessToken}} before running this folder. For the full request-storm version of this (many guides/tourists/tours at once, safe to run repeatedly), see scripts/request_storm.py in the repo instead - Postman is better for showing what one request looks like, the script is better for generating volume.

item.name: 1. Create tour (draft)

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Setnja kroz Petrovaradin",
  "description": "Obilazak tvrdjave i starog grada.",
  "difficulty": "easy",
  "tags": ["istorija", "arhitektura"],
  "durations": [{ "transport": "walk", "minutes": 60 }]
}

item.description: 403 here means the token isn't a guide - only guide/admin accounts can create tours.

item.name: 3. Add keypoint #2
item.description: Publishing needs at least 2 keypoints - this is the second one.

item.name: 4. Set price

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Setnja kroz Petrovaradin",
  "description": "Obilazak tvrdjave i starog grada.",
  "difficulty": "easy",
  "tags": ["istorija", "arhitektura"],
  "durations": [{ "transport": "walk", "minutes": 60 }],
  "price": 1200
}

item.description: Price isn't part of tour creation - it's set (or changed later) via this same update endpoint.

item.name: 5. Publish tour
item.description: One-way: a published tour can't be published again (400 "tour is not in draft status") - re-running this specific request twice is expected to fail the second time.

item.name: 6. Follow the guide (so a tourist can review later)
item.description: Following is idempotent - following someone you already follow just returns alreadyFollowing: true, never an error. Safe to run as many times as you like.

item.name: 2. Add tour to shopping cart
item.description: Needs firstTourId populated - run 'Browse published tours' first, and make sure at least one tour is published in this environment.

item.name: 4. Checkout (real purchase)
item.description: This actually completes a purchase against payments/Postgres and publishes purchase-completed to RabbitMQ - watch it show up on the Messaging & Databases Grafana dashboard and as a new trace in Jaeger.

item.name: 6. Leave a review
item.description: Gated two ways: 403 if you haven't purchased/executed this tour (run step 4 first), 400 "tourist has already reviewed this tour" if you run this twice for the same tour - one review per (tourist, tour) pair, by design.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Needs {{adminAccessToken}} set to an access token for an admin-role account (register/promote one, or log in as one, and paste its accessToken into this collection variable).
